extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common framework and parameterization. It represents mocap data as realistic 3D human meshes using the SMPL body model, making the dataset useful for animation, visualization, and training data generation.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Nikolaus F. Troje; Gerard Pons-Moll; Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by amassing 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets, downloading public datasets from the internet, obtaining some privately or recording them themselves, converting marker data into a common SMPL representation with MoSh++, and manually inspecting/correcting problematic mocap results. Additionally, a new synchronized scans-and-markers (SSM) dataset was recorded using an optical motion capture system synchronized with a high-resolution 4D body scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of sparse optical marker-based human motion capture markers from 15 mocap datasets; for the SSM dataset, raw data also included synchronized high-resolution 4D body scans captured with an optical mocap system and a 3dMD 4D scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing mocap datasets are described as limited in size, complexity, and motion diversity, and difficult to unify because of varying marker sets, formats, and body parameterizations. Prior retargeting approaches can fundamentally alter the original data.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape and motion data from human subjects; the dataset includes multiple subjects and preserves 3D body shape information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for machine learning research, especially training data for deep learning, as well as animation, visualization, computer vision, and generating synthetic training data. Users may use full body shape and soft-tissue information or ignore those components if only pose is needed.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community, and the authors plan to continue expanding it and support adding new captures when they can be shared similarly.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors split the newly collected SSM dataset into training and testing sets and sample 12 randomly chosen frames for model fitting.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: They unify 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common SMPL-based representation by converting sparse marker data into realistic 3D human meshes/body model parameters using MoSh++.

name.evidence: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes

description.evidence: we introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

creator.evidence: Naureen Mahmood ... Nima Ghorbani ... Nikolaus F. Troje ... Gerard Pons-Moll ... Michael J. Black

inLanguage.evidence: Large datasets are the cornerstone of recent advances in computer vision using deep learning.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “We amassed in total 15 mocap datasets... The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves... We used MoSh++ to map this large amount of marker data into our common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Due to inherent problems with mocap... we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “We amassed in total 15 mocap datasets... The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “The input is sparse markers and the output is SMPL body models.” and “To record this dataset we use an optical motion capture system synchronized and calibrated together with a high resolution 4D scanning system.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "existing mocap databases are insufficient in terms of size and complexity to exploit the full power of existing deep learning tools"; "datasets vary in the format of the data and the kinematic structure of the body, making it hard for researchers to combine them"; "This retargeting involves an inverse kinematics optimization that fundamentally changes the original data."

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: "AMASS has 42 hours of mocap, 346 subjects, and 11451 motions"; "SMPL provides the unifying representation that is independent of the marker set, yet maintains the richness of the original marker data, including the 3D body shape."

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: "The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning."; "enabling new applications that require large amounts of training data"; "This is useful for many tasks, including generating synthetic training for computer vision tasks"; "Users who only care about pose can ignore body shape and soft tissue deformations if they wish."

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: "will be publicly available to the research community"; "With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset. We make AMASS available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared."

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: "We separate the sequences into training and testing sets"; "In the first stage, for F = 12 randomly chosen frames"

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: "we introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization"; "MoSh++ ... converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model"
